target_customer: Online shoppers using a browser extension for one-click checkout and cashback, monetized through retailer commissions; later consumer businesses and browser developers
problem: Filling out checkout forms is slow and shoppers miss savings, while retailers lose sales at checkout.
business_model: Affiliate commission from retail partners shared with shoppers as cashback; later white-label browser extensions and shopping page intelligence for partners
product_category: Consumer fintech and ecommerce browser extension, shopping automation

founders.name: Adam MacEachern
founders.background_notes: Started the company with college roommates Daniel Baum and Palmer McCutcheon, per search coverage of the TechCrunch story.

founders.name: Daniel Baum
founders.background_notes: Previously a corporate lawyer per the YC page; other sources call him CTO.

founders.name: Palmer McCutcheon
founders.background_notes: Software engineer at Microsoft per the YC page.

competitors.name: Karma
competitors.what: AI shopping assistant browser extension that finds coupons and deals across the pre-purchase journey
competitors.funding_then: Raised a 25 million dollar Series A in October 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser extension that autofills checkout and classifies shopping pages is standard web engineering, with some difficulty in handling many different retailer checkouts and payments.

defensibility.rationale: Coupon and one-click checkout extensions were widely copyable, with larger players such as Honey and Capital One Shopping already distributed, and the product depends on browser stores and retailer affiliate terms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Funded checkout and coupon players kept the market, and Sleek ended with a team acquisition by ZeroClick in September 2025 after pivoting toward browser automation and AI.

market_need_then: Online shopping volume was elevated after 2020 and checkout friction and cashback extensions were popular. Dated evidence beyond competitor funding such as Karma raising 25 million dollars in October 2021 was not collected.

branding.domain_note: Used onsleek.com and later onsleek.ai, not sleek.com.

identity.visual_style: Minimal and friendly, lowercase accents, illustrated shop mockup
identity.voice_and_tone: Light and simple, tagline A smarter way through the web

brand_strength.rationale: A pleasant but common word shared with many other products named Sleek, and no sources show press about the brand, merch or community.

pivots.from: Consumer one-click checkout and cashback extension
pivots.to: White-label browser extensions and AI agents that understand shopping pages
pivots.why: The YC page and the company site describe browser automation and AI agents for consumer businesses, the reason is not stated in sources found.

outcome_analysis: Sleek launched a one-click checkout and cashback extension in the crowded shopping extension market, raised about 1.7 million dollars in 2022 from YC, Hyde Park, Fiat and Goodwater, and later repositioned toward browser automation and white-label extensions. In September 2025 ZeroClick acquired it and the founders and team joined ZeroClick, which looks like a small team landing rather than a scaled outcome. Terms are not public.
notes: Seed amount is 1.7 million dollars per TechCrunch and a seed database, another aggregator says 2 million; investor lists differ across aggregators and the TechCrunch list is used. Seed date shown as March 2022 from the article, one database dates it January 2022. Founder titles conflict between sources for Baum (COO or CTO). The product at founding was a consumer checkout extension; the YC description of browser automation reflects later positioning. Rating of failure factors is a judgment from thin sources. Only Karma had a source dated near the batch for competition; Ownit, Bolt and others appear only in the 2022 article.
